name: Renewable diesel and SAF by hydrotreated esters and fatty acids (HEFA)
applications: renewable naphtha and propane for chemicals
principle: Waste fats, used cooking oil and vegetable oils are pretreated to remove metals and phosphorus, then hydrotreated to strip oxygen and make straight-chain paraffins. A second step isomerises and, for jet, mildly cracks them to meet cold-flow specifications, and the products are fractionated into renewable diesel, SAF, naphtha and propane.

costs.metric: minimum jet fuel selling price, HEFA
costs.basis: Tao et al. 2017 open-access NREL-led TEA; range across five lipid feedstocks (waste oils lowest, dedicated lipid crops highest); 10% IRR discounted cash flow

source.note: Tao et al., Techno-economic and resource analysis of hydroprocessed renewable jet fuel, Biotechnology for Biofuels 10:262 (2017); salaries inflated to 2014 dollars; full text in corpus/nrel/
